reference: Heitjan, D. F. and Rubin, D. B. Ignorability and Coarse Data. Annals of Statistics 19(4), 1991.
result: Coarsening at random (CAR): the coarsening mechanism may be ignored for likelihood and Bayesian inference when the data are CAR and the parameters of the data and the coarsening process are distinct.
assumptions: Discrete sample space; coarsening variable distribution does not depend on the unobserved ideal outcome except through the observed coarse data; distinct parameters.
closest_csia_statement: C2 (exogeneity): w_h constant in h implies p = q.
subsumes: LIKELY YES for the ignorability direction
difference: CSIA's coarsening mechanism is a DESIGNED component of the diagnostic system rather than a feature of the data collection, and its non-ignorability is a static property of the signature table. The condition itself appears to be theirs.
claim_consequence: C2 must be labelled KNOWN and cite this. The candidate contribution is the runtime/static-checkability reading, not the condition.
